'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Cristina Calderón]], the last full-blooded [[Yahgan people|Yahgan]] and last native speaker of the [[Yahgan language]], dies in [[Chile]]. [https://www.france24.com/es/minuto-a-minuto/20220216-muere-en-chile-cristina-calder%C3%B3n-la-%C3%BAltima-hablante-del-pueblo-yag%C3%A1n (France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Brazil floods and landslides]]
**[[2022 Petrópolis floods]]
***At least 117 people are killed by [[Mudflow|mudslides]] and [[Flood|flooding]] in [[Petrópolis]], [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]]. It is the heaviest rainfall registered in the city since [[1932]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/death-toll-brazils-petropolis-rises-104-after-heavy-rains-2022-02-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[List of fatal shark attacks in Australia]]
**A man is killed in a [[shark attack]] off [[Little Bay, New South Wales|Little Bay]], [[Sydney]], [[Australia]]. It is the first fatal shark attack in Sydney since [[1963]]. A witness estimated that the shark was about {{convert|4.5|m|feet}} in length. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/shark-attack-kills-swimmer-sydney-bay-2022-02-16/ (Reuters)]
*At least 13 people are killed after [[wedding]] guests fall into a well in [[Kushinagar]], [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/02/17/india/india-deaths-well-collapse-kushinagar-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 64,718 new [[COVID-19]] cases, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4.96 million. ***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 27,831 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.11 million. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2022/02/16/covid-19-new-record-high-of-27831-cases-reported-wednesday-feb-16-says-health-dg#:~:text=PETALING%20JAYA%3A%20Malaysia%20recorded%20a,asymptomatic%20or%20suffering%20mild%20symptoms. ***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record 90,443 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.55 million. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/south-korea-covid-19-record-cases-baseball-league-suspended-2501136 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
***[[Switzerland]] lifts almost all of its COVID-19-related restrictions, with people no longer needing to show [[COVID-19 vaccine card|COVID-19 vaccine certificates]] to enter public venues, due to confidence that infection rates had been uncoupled from hospitalization. [https://www.politico.eu/article/switzerland-lifts-almost-all-covid-19-restrictions/ (''Politico.eu'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Rule of Law Conditionality Regulation]]
**The [[European Court of Justice]] dismisses [[Poland]] and [[Hungary]]'s challenges against the regulation and confirms that the regulation is in compliance with the [[treaties of the European Union]]. This will allow the [[European Commission]] to suspend funds from the [[EU budget]] to [[member state of the European Union|member states]] that have [[rule of law]] issues which are likely to affect the [[management]] of [[European Union|EU]] funds. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/2/16/poland-hungary-lose-legal-challenge-against-eu-rule-of-law-tool (Al Jazeera)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Philippine Basketball Association]]
**The [[Alaska Aces (PBA)|Alaska Aces]], the second most successful team in the history of the league with 14 championship titles in 35 years, announced that it will cease to exist after the conclusion of the ongoing [[2021 PBA Governors' Cup]]. [https://www.espn.com.au/basketball/pba/story/_/id/33301118/alaska-aces-depart-philippine-basketball-association-14-titles-35-years (ESPN)]
